items.q: Will you upgrade another maker’s system?
items.a: For [makes and equipment types serviced]: we assess it, then add or replace modules from our package. Without drawings, we walk the system down and measure dead legs. Polypropylene (PP) joins other piping by [tie-in method to existing piping]. A hot-held loop, or routine 80 °C sanitization at loop pressure, needs polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) or stainless [whether we quote PVDF].

items.q: Will an upgrade restart our performance qualification (PQ)?
items.a: Not necessarily. After a change, WHO TRS 1033 (11.3) sizes performance qualification (PQ) by documented risk assessment: phases, length and sampling. EU good manufacturing practice (GMP) Annex 15 puts the change through change control. Health Canada’s GUI-0029 adds that several minor changes can make a major one. Your quality unit decides; we draft the rationale.

items.q: Can we keep producing water during the upgrade?
items.a: Yes, for generation, pretreatment and capacity upgrades. Each new module goes in beside the old one and is tied in during a short shutdown. If your tank cannot cover it, plan temporary water: [temporary RO or EDI units, flow L/h]. A loop replacement needs a planned shutdown.
